title: Ladakh to Launch India’s First High-Altitude Wildlife Safari
summary: Ladakh approved India’s first guided high-altitude wildlife safari on 6 August 2026. The plan covers snow-leopard and bird-watching trails in Hemis National Park, Changthang, Karakoram Wildlife Sanctuary, Nubra, Zanskar, Sham, Kargil and Dr...

blocks.content: Ladakh approved India’s first guided high-altitude wildlife safari on 6 August 2026. The plan covers snow-leopard and bird-watching trails in Hemis National Park, Changthang, Karakoram Wildlife Sanctuary, Nubra, Zanskar, Sham, Kargil and Drass.

items: Hemis National Park is one of the key habitats of the snow leopard in India.
Changthang and Karakoram are important high-altitude wildlife zones in Ladakh.
Open-back jeep safaris are used in several Indian protected areas for regulated wildlife viewing.
Snow leopard is listed as a threatened big cat species in high-altitude ecosystems of the Himalayas.
